rationale: The reviewer found that 70 of 100 test promoters are near-copies of training sequences (64 at ≥95% identity, 6 more at 90–95%), with accuracy 1.00 on those versus 0.50 on the 30 novel ones, which matches the key. They also proposed clustering with MMseqs2/CD-HIT, re-splitting by cluster and reporting novel-subset accuracy. Their other points (missing baselines, the 'regulatory grammar' overclaim, a single run) are generic or follow from the leakage, so they don't count as separate key-absent issues.
